The martingale lot multiplication and the 500-line hard-coded balance-to-lot lookup table make reliable Python conversion risky and broker-dependent.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: When AutoLot=true, base lot is determined by a hard-coded balance-to-lot lookup table (LotSize function, ~0.01 per $273 balance increment). After a loss (balance below stored globalBalans), the lot is multiplied by BigLotSize (default 6x). OneMult=true means the multiplied lot persists until a profitable trade restores balance; OneMult=false applies multiplication cumulatively to each new position.

custom_logic_notes: Dead code bug: SignalOpenSell has a second return statement (return false) on line 190 that is unreachable since line 189 always returns first. This means the sell signal always evaluates op1[0]-op2[0]>_Point*Delta_S and never falls through to false. The EA uses global variables (GlobalVariableSet/Get) to persist balance and lot state across EA restarts, keyed by program name + symbol + period + account + trade mode. DeleteGV only cleans these during testing. The LotSize() function is a ~500-line hard-coded if-chain mapping account balance thresholds to specific lot values (non-linear, not a simple formula). Trade entry is gated by dt.hour==TradeTime (default 14), meaning trades only open during a single hour each day. MaxOpenTime forces position close after 504 hours (21 days) default. SL/TP validation checks against broker StopsLevel before placing orders.
python_conversion_notes: The LotSize() balance-to-lot lookup table must be faithfully transcribed as a data structure (dict or list of thresholds). The martingale logic with BigLotSize multiplier and OneMult flag requires careful state management - must track previous balance and lot size across trades. Global variable persistence (gvp prefix) maps to a file-based or database state store in Python. The time filter allows entry only during TradeTime hour (14 by default), which is broker-server-time dependent. The deviation of Sym.Spread()*3 for order slippage must be approximated in Python backtesting. The SignalOpenSell dead code (unreachable return false on line 190) should be cleaned up but does not affect behavior. SL/TP use Sym.Point() not _Point, meaning symbol-specific point value from CSymbolInfo - must use correct symbol point value in Python. No digit adjustment is needed since Point()*StopLossPoints already handles 5-digit brokers correctly.
